## How a schema is read

Each member of a scalar type is a `field` line; members of nested objects have dotted paths.
An array is a `group` (engine-spec 0.7): items that are objects are walked as a message is,
with paths relative to the item; items of a scalar type are one `.` line. `allOf`, `oneOf`
and `anyOf` contribute the members of every branch, merged by name; `null` among the
types means the member may be absent. Types: string `string`, integer `int`, number
`float` (`int` when the schema states `multipleOf: 1`), boolean `bool`. A `date-time`
string is kept as text in its raw key, so it round-trips as written.

Residue (engine-spec 0.5): a scalar member no line maps, at any depth of nested objects, is
carried back; arrays no group maps, and anything inside them, are not.

Limits of this pack: objects nested deeper than 10 levels (an array counts as a level) are not mapped (the deepest VSS signals sit below the instance levels; the limit keeps every signal of the tree and no more). Such a place is in the table under Not mapped;
outside an array its scalars are residue and round-trip, inside an array they are dropped.

## Mapped to shared keys

| Kind | Path | Key | Schema type | Evidence (in this project's words; the notes name the source) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle` | `Vehicle.CurrentLocation.Latitude` | `lat` (float, deg) | number | spec/Vehicle/Vehicle.vspec: latitude of the GNSS antenna in WGS 84 geodetic coordinates, degrees |
| `vehicle` | `Vehicle.CurrentLocation.Longitude` | `lon` (float, deg) | number | spec/Vehicle/Vehicle.vspec: longitude of the GNSS antenna in WGS 84 geodetic coordinates, degrees |
| `vehicle` | `Vehicle.CurrentLocation.Timestamp` | `time_ms` (int, ms) | string, date-time | spec/Vehicle/Vehicle.vspec: the GNSS time of the current location, a string in ISO 8601 with the UTC time zone |
| `vehicle` | `Vehicle.Speed` | `speed_ms` (float, m/s) | number, read with `scale:5/18` | spec/Vehicle/Vehicle.vspec: the vehicle's speed in km/h; read as speed_ms with scale:5/18 (1 km/h = 5/18 m/s) |

Each bound path also has its raw key on a second line (ruling 16 of 0.5): the shared
key first, so encode writes the shared value when the entity has it.

A path read with a float `scale` has its raw key's line first instead: the scaled value
does not always return the number as written, so a same-format round trip writes the raw
key, and an entity from another format, which has only the shared key, gets the scaled one.

## Keys and lists

Module `vssvehicle`: 14 keys, 2 lists. A key is named by its path (`a.b` is `a_b`; inside a list, the
list name comes first). Names are pinned in `tools/gen/names/vss-vehicle.json`: a later run keeps every
existing name and only adds new ones.

## Vectors

One same-format round trip per kind, computed by the generator's own json codec (no engine):
every mapped place holds a value, an array has two items (one inside an item), the input is
canonical, so the expected output is the input.
